Yes. Hansen Global Forest Change (GFC-2025-v1.13) records 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 within the property, about 2.23% of its 3,643.5 ha.

Context from the other sources:
- JRC's 2020 forest map shows 98% of the loss area was forest in 2020.
- The MGAP 2021 forest map classes 68.1 ha of it as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). None is native forest, and 13.2 ha lies outside mapped forest.
- The loss is corroborated: later years of the series were observed (through 2025), and JRC agrees well above the 50% threshold.

An additional 37.3 ha of 2021 loss occurred in patches under 0.5 ha. It is not counted in the 81.3 ha.

Because most of the loss is in planted pine, it likely reflects plantation harvest rather than native-forest clearing. Hansen loss does not by itself show the cause.
